title: New footing and an earlier image

captions.physics: Reflecting on experience and explaining structure
captions.emotions: Saying farewell to an earlier image

meaning: Your shared view can gain dependable grounds even when an understandable explanation requires releasing a valued earlier image.
text: A dependable explanation sometimes comes with regret for an earlier image. The Hermit in the physical position of Ajna suggests reflecting on experience and sharing a clear understanding of structure. The Emperor in energy supports seeking stable grounds for your shared view. Death in emotions experiences farewell to an earlier picture. Both of you may already understand the new explanation while the old one remains dear. Your view gains firmer footing, while a sense of loss concerns one particular image that no longer describes the whole structure.

For example, you examine a small patterned wooden box. Its entire surface seemed carved from one piece. After considering the joints carefully, one person explains how separate pieces form the pattern. **New footing can appear alongside farewell to an earlier image.** The structure becomes clearer. Yet you miss the appealing idea of a single piece of wood. Regret does not erase the recognised joints, nor must it immediately become admiration for another way of working. Both layers can still appear in your conversation.

The risk is treating emotional farewell as refusing the explanation and proving an already understood connection again. Precision is lost behind a demand for the right response. Wanting stable grounds distinguishes knowledge from feeling: the new structure is already accessible to both while the earlier image gradually loses its attraction.
